lifecycle_contract.output_bound: n + ceil(n/8); every literal costs 9 bits and every reference costs 17 bits for at least 3 bytes
lifecycle_contract.finalize: REQUIRED_NOOP_ONE_SHOT_FINALIZE; upstream bitfile flush occurs in EncodeLZSS
lifecycle_contract.reset: NEW_CONTEXT_PER_OBJECT; ABI reset clears state and timing

stream_components.outer_container: 12-byte unique prefix plus canonical dtype/shape/name/track descriptors
stream_components.raw_format: MSB-first bit I/O; literal 1+8 bits; reference 0 then offset low byte + offset high nibble + 4-bit adjusted length on the qualified little-endian host
stream_components.dictionary: fixed 4096-byte space-filled window; binary-tree matcher; no external bits
stream_components.padding: 0..7 zero low bits, independently inspected and charged
stream_components.decode_validation: exact token coverage and decoded length before the EOF-tolerant upstream decoder
stream_components.accounting: exact token, padding, descriptor and prefix bits from the finalized physical stream

known_limitations: This is an explicitly requested independent C LZSS AlgorithmID, not the spreadsheet-selected alexkazik/lzss implementation; results must not be merged or directly ranked as the same implementation.
Fixed offset12/length4, space-filled 4096-byte window, binary-tree matcher, scalar single-thread execution only.
Upstream compressor and matcher use static global work state, so concurrent calls in one process are forbidden.
The vendored 12-file closure remains byte-identical. A hashed build patch removes binary-tree sentinel out-of-bounds accesses; patched/unmodified release streams match on 48 retained cases.

The ABI emits/accepts the canonical empty stream without entering upstream bitfile code because upstream EncodeLZSS leaks its bitfile wrapper on the empty-input early return and zero-length fmemopen behavior differed under sanitizer.
No checksum: structurally valid corruption may decode; benchmark common bit-exact validation remains mandatory.
GRUB is decode-only and uses grouped flag bytes, so it is reference-only and is not linked or claimed byte-compatible.
The shared Python LZSS container/session machinery is implementation-neutral preparation for a future C-only migration; Rust lzss-raw remains registered and all prior evidence stays append-only.
